# F18 + F19 — the Linguaskill pair · ⚠️ THEY CANNIBALISE EACH OTHER

- **F18** `src/pages/blog/cambridge-vs-linguaskill-diferencias.astro` +
  `pages/blog/CambridgeVsLinguaskillDiferenciasPage.tsx` (442 lines) — **132 imp, 0 clicks**
- **F19** `src/pages/blog/certificado-linguaskill.astro` +
  `pages/blog/CertificadoLinguaskillPage.tsx` (448 lines) — **111 imp, 0 clicks**

Both rank for the same queries, one of them from nowhere:

| query | F18 | F19 |
|---|---|---|
| `diferencias entre linguaskill y cambridge` | **17.6** | 84.4 |
| `cambridge linguaskill` | 27.2 | 38.6 |
| `linguaskill` | 36.1 | **2.2** |

**The decision is made. Do not re-open it:**

- **F19 `certificado-linguaskill` owns the head term `linguaskill`** — it ranks **2.2**. It becomes
  the definitive "what the Linguaskill is, what it certifies, how it works" page.
- **F18 `cambridge-vs-linguaskill-diferencias` owns the comparison** — it ranks **17.6** for
  `diferencias entre linguaskill y cambridge`. It stays a comparison and stops trying to be an
  explainer.

**The fix on each:**

- **F18:** cut or compress any general "what is the Linguaskill" explanation down to two sentences
  and **link to F19**. Strengthen the comparison itself: format, timing, cost, results speed (48
  hours), who accepts each, and which one suits which goal. Add the `cambridge linguaskill` phrasing.
- **F19:** cut or compress any head-to-head comparison down to two sentences and **link to F18**.
  Strengthen the head-term coverage: what the certificate is, what it proves, whether it expires,
  the CEFR mapping, that Impulse is an **official Linguaskill centre** so it is prepared *and sat*
  here — which is a genuine differentiator against a Cambridge exam.

That single reciprocal-link decision is the highest-value thing in this window.
